chapter_title: Chương 277: 0279 【Đại Ngũ Mao đến Hải Nội Võng】

segments.title: Chương 277: 0279 【Đại Ngũ Mao đến Hải Nội Võng】
segments.content:
With the home purchase contract signed, both parties agreed to formally transfer the ownership after the National Day holiday.

Watching Liu Jianguo drive away, Bian Guanyue asked curiously, "Since he was one of Baidu's earliest employees, he should have some stock options, right? Why would he sell his house to start a business?"

"What he has isn't just options, but actual shares from the very beginning," Chen Guiliang estimated in his head. "If converted to RMB, Liu Jianguo's Baidu stock is worth at least two or three hundred million. But this isn't a good year to cash out."

Even after the dilution from the IPO and subsequent offerings, Liu Jianguo still held a hefty 0.9% of Baidu's shares.

According to stock market rules, he could have started cashing out as early as February this year.

But at that time, venture capital firms like IDG, along with employee shares and options, were being sold off en masse. During the most intense period of selling, the stock price plummeted by 40% in a single week.

Just as Baidu's stock price recovered, the "Surging Ad Traffic Scandal" broke out in May, and many institutions took the opportunity to short-sell and stir up trouble, causing a panicked sell-off among investors. In July, the "Layoff Scandal" emerged, which also affected Baidu's stock price.

When the second lock-up period ended in August, venture capitalists and employees began another round of selling.

The selling is still ongoing.

In the first nine months of this year, Baidu's stock price fluctuated dramatically. At its lowest, it was $43; at its highest, $86. It kept going back and forth, up and down.

Liu Jianguo was probably still testing the waters and wouldn't be touching his Baidu stock anytime soon.

Chen Guiliang drove Bian Guanyue back to school, chatting about the house along the way. Their conversation focused on whether or not to redecorate.

According to Liu Jianguo, he owned many properties in Beijing, including three in Huaqing Jiayuan alone. The one he sold to Chen Guiliang had been bought from a property flipper last year, and he had originally intended to renovate it and live in it himself.

Now, just two months after the renovation was completed, while the place was still airing out, he sold it to Chen Guiliang.

It was essentially a new home, never lived in for a single day.

"Let's see," Bian Guanyue said. "Since no one has lived there and it was just renovated, I don't think it's necessary to go through all that trouble again."

Chen Guiliang said, "He mentioned the decor is more Chinese-style, which might seem a bit old-fashioned for young people. The rooftop garden also has a Chinese-style small bridge and flowing water. I'm afraid you won't like it."

Bian Guanyue smiled. "You forget I studied Sichuan opera when I was a child. I love those kinds of ancient gardens."

"Then let's get a Beijing siheyuan when we have the time," Chen Guiliang said.

"Okay," Bian Guanyue said, even more delighted. She had no idea how valuable a Beijing siheyuan was.

The price of Beijing siheyuan was currently in a period of rapid growth, but it was still relatively cheap compared to post-2010.

But they were very difficult to buy.

Most Beijing siheyuan had unclear property rights, and one could easily fall into a trap. It was even possible that after the ownership transfer, a "previous owner" would suddenly appear, or it would be reported as a protected cultural heritage site.

Chen Guiliang didn't have the spare time to get involved in such troublesome matters.

After dropping Bian Guanyue off at the school gate, they shared a kiss in the car and exchanged a few more sweet nothings before Bian Guanyue got out and waved goodbye.

Chen Guiliang drove back to the company.

Huang Xinyuan, the head of ByteDance's SP business department, had been waiting for him for a long time and immediately followed him into his office to report on his work.

"The Online Original Music Contest is going very well. The results will be announced after the National Day holiday, and I've already taken a liking to several of the entries," Huang Xinyuan said. "Over the past half month, I've flown to several provinces, drinking with department heads from China Mobile and China Unicom every day. I've basically reconnected with all my old contacts. 'Wait One Minute' is about to hit a massive boom in ringtone downloads."

Chen Guiliang offered words of comfort and praise, "You've really worked hard. All that flying around and drinking must be tough."

Huang Xinyuan sighed. "We're in a very bad period. The state has already started to get serious about cleaning up the chaos on the internet this year, and that includes rectifying the SP business. And SP is a top priority."

Chen Guiliang asked, "What's the specific situation?"

"I found all this out while drinking with the leaders from China Mobile and China Unicom," Huang Xinyuan said. "In June this year, the higher-ups officially issued a document. But it concerns the interests of Mobile, Unicom, and many internet companies, so everyone has been trying to delay as much as possible. Now, we can't delay any longer. The higher-ups have set a final deadline: the policy must be implemented by December! I estimate that all companies involved in the SP business will be summoned for talks one by one in October. Or, they might just hold a collective meeting to talk to everyone at once."

Chen Guiliang asked, "Are the measures just the ones mentioned in the document?"

"Yes, they all have to be fully implemented," Huang Xinyuan nodded.

Chen Guiliang smiled. "In any case, our principle is not to engage in trap consumption. If the policy is implemented, then no one can do it anymore, which is actually fairer for us."

Huang Xinyuan looked miserable. "This affects more than just trap consumption. Normal consumption will also be disrupted by the two-step verification."

Among the rectification measures introduced by the central government, the most important one was that SP services must have "two-step verification."

Many users, while playing on their phones, would make a purchase by accident and not even know what they had bought. Such cases were extremely common, and the complaint hotlines were ringing off the hook every day.

Implementing "two-step verification" in the future would prevent accidental purchases.

But there was an even more serious impact: some impulse buyers would regret their decision during the second confirmation step and cancel their recent impulsive action.

This one "two-step verification" policy from the central government could cut the revenue of many internet companies in half! This was especially true for mobile portal websites like Kong.net.

Furthermore, there was also a 24-hour refund policy, which, in theory, could even give rise to users who get services for free. China Mobile and China Unicom would surely try to obstruct this in every possible way, resorting to all sorts of tricks when implementing it.

It had been three months since the policy was announced, and everyone had been dragging their feet on implementation. The relevant central departments were finally about to set a deadline.

As a consumer, one would certainly support it wholeheartedly.

But one's position determines one's perspective. No matter how principled Chen Guiliang was, he still felt a little uncomfortable—he didn't support trap consumption, but he did support impulse buying!

Chen Guiliang said, "Regardless, the central government's efforts to regulate the internet are beneficial for the long-term healthy development of the industry. We'll just follow whatever the policy says."

Huang Xinyuan didn't know whether to laugh or cry, and offered some casual flattery, "Boss, you're the one with the right attitude."

At this point, having the right attitude or not didn't matter. You couldn't go against the central government.

Huang Xinyuan finally got to the point. "Boss, I think the content on Hainei.com's WAP site is still insufficient. I want to add a games section."

"Mobile games?" Chen Guiliang asked.

Huang Xinyuan nodded. "Kong.net's mobile games are extremely profitable."

The JAVA and BREW games of the feature phone era were truly a blind spot in Chen Guiliang's knowledge.

Not only had he never seen them, he had barely even heard of them.

Huang Xinyuan said, "I've looked into it. Most of Kong.net's mobile games are licensed versions of old foreign mobile games. We can license them too, and the fees aren't too expensive. In addition, we can also develop our own mobile games, or have your company, Youke, develop them for us."

"Are they really that profitable?" Chen Guiliang asked.

Huang Xinyuan said, "About 25% of Kong.net's revenue comes from various mobile games."

Chen Guiliang made a decision on the spot. "Let's do as you say. We'll license most of the games directly, and I'll have Youke develop a few."

The mobile games developed by Youke would naturally be sold to ByteDance's WAP site for a fee.

He would hire more people for Youke to specialize in mobile games.

The graphics of mobile games back then were somewhat similar to the old Nintendo Entertainment System and early PC standalone games.

Chen Guiliang had already thought of the first project: a mobile version of *My Own Swordsman*.

This would, of course, be different from the MMORPG Feng Ji was making. The mobile version would only feature scenes from the *My Own Swordsman* TV series. The player would control a pixelated character using the feature phone's various keys, walking around to accept quests and fight monsters.

On a weekday, Chen Guiliang donated the book, *A Record of Things Seen and Heard About River Defenses*, to Peking University.

It wasn't a major cultural relic or a valuable item, so the standard procedure was followed. He even received a donation certificate.
